tools.name: find_powered_land
tools.description: Search for land parcels in Texas that sit close to a high-voltage substation: powered land for data centers, battery storage, crypto mining or other large loads. Filter by county or by a point and radius, minimum acreage, maximum distance to a substation and minimum substation voltage. Returns parcel acreage, location, property ID, situs address, legal description and appraisal values, and the nearest qualifying substation with its owner. Filter by owner type (company, individual, trust_estate, public, private), and by max_wetland_pct to drop parcels that are largely mapped wetland (USFWS NWI), and by bus_kv_max or osm_class to keep parcels whose nearest substation has a lower-voltage or distribution bus mapped in OpenStreetMap. Set group_by_owner to roll parcels up by landowner and rank owners by total acres near qualifying substations, e.g. 'who controls 200+ acres within a mile of a 138 kV substation'; undivided-interest accounts on the same polygon are counted once. Enterprise Lite and Enterprise: below them it returns the count of qualifying parcels and their acreage, not the parcels or owners. Parcel coverage is limited to the counties listed in the response.

min_parcel_acres.description: With group_by_owner: smallest parcel counted toward an owner's total. Default 5, minimum 1 (below 5 acres the radius is capped at 10 miles).

bus_kv_max.description: Keep parcels whose nearest qualifying substation has a bus at or below this kV (lowest mapped OpenStreetMap voltage, else the listed kV). A 345/138/69 kV station passes bus_kv_max 69 even though min_kv judges it by its top voltage. Not used with group_by_owner.

osm_class.description: Keep parcels whose nearest qualifying substation has this OpenStreetMap class. distribution means a distribution bus is mapped. Stations not mapped in OpenStreetMap are dropped. Not used with group_by_owner.

min_flat_pct.description: Enterprise. Minimum percent of the parcel under 5 percent slope (USGS 3DEP). Adds flat_pct, mean_slope_pct and wells_active to each parcel.

same_side_of_rail.description: Enterprise. Keep only parcels with no active railroad between the parcel and its own nearest qualifying substation (straight line, TxDOT/FRA rail). Every parcel then carries rail_crossings and rail_lines.

measure_terrain.description: Enterprise. Add flat_pct, mean_slope_pct and wells_active without filtering.

max_dist_line_mi.description: Enterprise. Keep parcels whose centroid is within this many miles of a distribution line under 69 kV (OpenStreetMap mapped, plus the gridfinder model unless dist_mapped_only). For small loads and distribution-connected solar or storage, typically under 10 MW. Adds nearest_dist_line_mi and dist_line_basis. Measured on the first 80 parcels after the other filters.

dist_mapped_only.description: Enterprise. With max_dist_line_mi, count only lines traced in OpenStreetMap, not modeled ones. Mapped coverage is thin in many counties.

max_fiber_mi.description: Enterprise. Keep parcels within this many miles of a mapped fiber route (provider GIS or carrier corridor). Adds nearest_fiber_mi and nearest_fiber_provider. Measured on the first 80 parcels after the other filters.

max_gas_mi.description: Enterprise. Keep parcels within this many miles of a mapped natural gas pipeline (RRC; see min_gas_diameter_in and gas_interstate). Straight-line distance to the mapped line. Not used with group_by_owner.

min_gas_diameter_in.description: Enterprise. Only count gas lines of at least this diameter in inches (for example 12) when measuring nearest_gas_mi.

gas_interstate.description: Enterprise. Only count interstate (FERC regulated) or intrastate (Railroad Commission regulated) gas lines. Default all.

tools.name: heavy_haul
tools.description: Enterprise. Routes an oversize or heavy truck load to a Texas site and flags what is on the way, from federal and state public data. Origin defaults to the nearest port; or pass origin as nearest_intermodal, nearest_transload, or an origin address or coordinate (a town the load ships from). The route is a truck route on OpenStreetMap (Valhalla) that honors mapped height, width and weight limits for the load given. Along it: FHWA National Bridge Inventory bridges within 25 m that are posted, restricted or closed, have clearance under the load height plus 1 ft, or have an operating rating under the load weight; TxGIO low-water crossings within 50 m (inventory about 2010); and, on the last miles to the site, local roads, minor collectors and lanes under 11 ft from FHWA HPMS 2024. No permit, escort or cost figures: TxDMV routes every oversize or overweight permit, and a heavy-haul carrier confirms the route.

tools.name: haul_compare
tools.description: Enterprise. Compares ways to move a heavy load to a Texas site from an origin (default the nearest port; or a Texas town, address or point): (1) truck direct on the truck router, (2) truck to the nearest active rail line, rail on the FRA North American Rail Network to the rail-served transload or intermodal terminal nearest the site, then truck to the site. Gives miles per leg, railroads on the rail leg and how many times the line changes railroad, and an indicative linehaul cost per option from published national averages (BTS NTS Table 3-21 revenue per ton-mile: truck 27.07 cents 2022, Class I rail 5.19 cents 2023; ATRI 2025 truck operating cost $2.336 per mile). The averages are general freight, not oversize permit loads, and exclude transload handling, switching, permits, escorts and rigging, so use them to rank options, not to budget. (3) truck to the nearest dock, barge on the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, ship channels and connected rivers to the dock nearest the site, then truck (BTS domestic water 3.84 cents per ton-mile, 2022). Docks are USACE navigation units; confirm one handles project cargo. Run heavy_haul on the truck legs for bridges and low-water crossings.

The groundwater district's adopted rules (exempt-well limits, permits, spacing, production caps per acre, export rules, fees, metering) with rule numbers, pages and short quotes, where two independent extractions agreed; otherwise a link to the rules. Optional demand_mgd or demand_gpm returns how many wells at the local 75th percentile yield would meet it, and the acres of groundwater rights a per-acre district cap implies. Use when someone asks about water for a data center, cooling, a plant, irrigation or a well: how deep, how much, how salty, who regulates it. Driller yields are completion estimates, not long-term capacity; district permits decide what can be pumped. Free shows the aquifers, district and well counts; Pro adds yields, depths, quality, trends, district rules and the well list.

tools.name: water_well_plan
tools.description: Proposes a groundwater supply well for a Texas address or coordinate and grades nearby water buy areas, from public state well records (TWDB Groundwater Database and Submitted Drillers Reports) with every well assigned to a water-bearing unit (formation). Ranks the units under and around the point by grade, then for the best unit gives a proposed total depth and screen interval, expected yield (low, design and upside, weighted by test method), water quality (TDS with sample years), depth to water and level trend, annual yield per well and under the groundwater district's per-acre cap, wells needed for a demand, the analog wells it rests on, and a leave-one-out check of how well nearby wells predict each other. Buy-area grades: A = 75th percentile yield 300+ gpm, TDS under 1,000 mg/l, median depth 1,500 ft or less, water level falling no more than 1 ft/yr, 5+ analog wells; B = the same but TDS up to 3,000 or unknown; C = 130+ gpm with 3+ analogs. tools.description: Finds construction material on land near any Texas point: red select (red sandy clay select fill), sand, gravel, ironstone (iron ore gravel road material), caliche, limestone near the surface and roadfill, and every known pit, active and old. Returns: the soil and surface geology at the point with its material rating; pits within the radius (TCEQ-registered aggregate operations with operator, material and registration; USGS past producers; OpenStreetMap quarries; bare ground from 2001 and 2021 land cover that marks old or unregistered pits); market prices (TxDOT bid medians for the district: embankment fill and flexible base; landowner royalty and at-pit price references, each with its source); and ranked parcels of 10+ acres that carry the material, by default untapped ones with no pit yet, with material acres, red select depth, thickness, soil class and plasticity, caliche and limestone depth, appraised land $/acre, distance from the point, the nearest pit of the same material, and a dirt value range: landowner royalty and operator sales at the pit for the in-place red select volume, or per acre-foot where the soil survey gives no thickness. Use for 'where can I find red select near Tyler', 'caliche pit land near Midland', 'borrow pit for my pad', 'old gravel pits near here', 'what is the dirt on this tract worth'. Soil survey ratings cover the top 1.5 to 2 m and map soil associations, not every acre: confirm with test pits, lab gradation and plasticity, and a TCEQ APO registration before mining. Enterprise; free and Pro get counts.

address.description: Texas street address, e.g. '1201 Main St, Houston, TX'. Use this or lat/lng.

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Use with lng instead of address.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Use with lat instead of address.

material.description: Material to rank parcels by. Default any (each parcel's best material).

radius_mi.description: Search radius in miles. Default 15, max 40.

status.description: untapped (default): parcels with the material and no known pit or bare ground; pit: parcels that already have one; all.

min_material_acres.description: Least acres of the material on the parcel. Default 5.

royalty_usd_per_ton.description: Optional landowner royalty in $/ton the user supplies; replaces the cited royalty range in the dirt value.
